board: Connecticut State Board of Accountancy (Department of Consumer Protection)

cycle.note: Connecticut CPE years run July 1 – June 30. The report for each year is due the following December 31.

requirements.label: Annual CPE
requirements.note: 40 hours between July 1 and June 30, reported to the Board by December 31. Up to 20 extra hours from last year carry forward (a carryover can't be carried again).

requirements.label: Audit, attest or compilation
requirements.note: If you perform or supervise attest or compilation services, or sign financial statement reports: 8 of the 40 hours must have a field of study of Audit, Attest or Compilation — this year's hours only, not carryover (CT DCP Q&A). We count courses whose field of study is Auditing.

requirements.label: Governmental (Yellow Book audits)
requirements.note: Government auditors: 24 hours in government-related subjects every two years (GAO Yellow Book).

requirements.label: Ethics
requirements.note: 4 hours of ethics in every three CPE years.

newLicensee.note: No CPE report is required for the CPE year in which your license was first issued.

licenseDateHint: Connecticut CPE years run July 1 – June 30 regardless of this date; each year's report is due December 31.
issueDateHint: If your license was first issued during the current CPE year (since July 1), no CPE report is due for it.
limitsNotTracked: Instructor credit: max 20 hours a year (45 for teaching at educational institutions).
Peer review credit: max 16 hours a year.
Published articles/books: 10 per publication, 40 a year.
Technical meetings and non-qualifying programs: max 10 hours a year.
recordRetention: Keep documentation for at least 3 years from each program's completion.
toVerify: Ethics window: modelled as 4 hours in the current and two previous CPE years (the Board says the three-year clock resets when ethics is done early).
Both Regulatory and Behavioral Ethics count toward the 4 ethics hours ('a course which covers ethical behavior').
Connecticut license expiration timing — the app doesn't use it for CPE (the CPE year is fixed July–June).

Compilation courses: the Board requires a field of study of Audit, Attest or Compilation. NASBA certificates have no 'Compilation' field, so compilation courses printed as 'Accounting' aren't counted — the user can change the field to Auditing if the certificate supports it.
